data.name: Cornelia
data.long_meaning: The name Cornelia comes from the Roman name Cornelius, which means 'horn of the moon'. In Roman mythology, cornus was the name of the horned god and silva was the moon goddess. Cornelia is therefore interpreted as ‘horn of God’ or ‘horn of the moon goddess’. In Christianity, it was borne by several saints and martyrs, and is also associated with the Virgin Mary.
data.spiritual_meaning: A strong and powerful name, Cornelia symbolizes the strength and power of God and the protection and guidance of the Virgin Mary.

historical_references.reference: Cornelia, the daughter of Scipio Africanus, was a famous Roman matron and mother of the Gracchi brothers, Tiberius and Gaius. She was admired for her beauty, virtue, and nobility. Cornelia lived during the late Roman Republic, around the 2nd and 1st centuries BC.

historical_references.reference: Cornelia Ceres, also known as Cornelia the Wise, was a legendary Roman woman who lived during the early Roman Republic, around the 5th century BC. According to legend, she was the mother of the twin brothers Romulus and Remus who founded Rome. Cornelia was said to be a virtuous woman who raised her sons to become great leaders.
